column1: # Marathi (mr) catalog. Columns, separated by a TAB:  context <TAB> source <TAB> translation
#   context  empty                a plain UI string; `source` is the English text in the code
#            @id                  a command id (e.g. file.saveAs): wins over the English text for
#                                 that menu item, so one id can read differently from its twin
#                                 the language's forms separated by "|" (see `plural` in i18n/mod.rs)
#            anything else        a disambiguating context passed to `tr_ctx`
#   escapes  \n  \t  \\  inside a column. `{name}` placeholders must appear in both columns.
#   lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored.
# Clean-room: every entry was written from the plain meaning of the English label using ordinary
# modern Marathi computing and photo-editing vocabulary (लेयर, ब्रश, निवड, कॅनव्हास, जतन करा ...). No
# proprietary localisation resource, string table or product UI was consulted or copied; add
# entries the same way. Marathi shares the Devanagari script and many loanwords with Hindi; where a
# shared loanword fit naturally the choice was cross-checked against hi.tsv, but spelling (no nukta,
# ॅ for English "a" as in पॅनेल), vocabulary and grammar (करा, आणि, -चा/-ची/-चे, मध्ये) follow
# Marathi usage throughout, not Hindi's. Product and technology names (PhotoCraft, Photoshop, PSD,
# OpenType, CMYK, RGB, Lab ...) stay in Latin letters, as do key names, units and placeholders; the
# trailing "…" of dialog commands is kept.
# Marathi plural rule: one|other (one is n = 1).
# Machine-translated with Claude (Anthropic) for @tronicum; not yet reviewed by a native speaker.
